title: UA Local 597 (Pipefitters) — GAN Battery Practice Exam, Form A
confidenceNote: GAN is confirmed as the testing company by Local 597, and the section names come from the local’s own site. GAN does not publish per-section question counts or time limits, so the split used here is the one this exam was built with, not an official figure.

questions.explanation: 5 ÷ 16 = 0.3125. Halving 5/8 (0.625) gets you there too, since 5/16 is half of 5/8.
12.5% is 1/8. 96 ÷ 8 = 12. Converting the percent to a simple fraction is faster than decimal multiplication.

questions.stem: 28 is what percent of 80?
questions.explanation: 28 ÷ 80 = 0.35 = 35%. The number after "of" is always the bottom of the fraction.

questions.explanation: Convert everything to decimals: 0.600, 0.625, 0.580, 0.583. 5/8 = 0.625 wins.
Multiply straight across: 10/24, which reduces to 5/12. Cancelling the 2 into the 8 first is quicker.

Square the top and the bottom: 3² = 9 and 4² = 16, so 9/16. Squaring is not doubling.
10% is 24 and 5% is half of that, 12. Add: 36.

questions.stem: A run of pipe measures 24 ft 6 in. It is cut into 6 equal pieces. Ignoring the saw kerf, how long is each piece?
choices: 4 ft 1 in
4 ft 9 in
4 ft 6 in
3 ft 9 in
questions.explanation: Convert to inches first: 24 × 12 + 6 = 294 in. 294 ÷ 6 = 49 in = 4 ft 1 in.

questions.stem: Four fitters install 180 ft of pipe in 6 hours. What is the crew average per man-hour?
choices: 4.5 ft
7.5 ft
30 ft
questions.explanation: Man-hours = 4 × 6 = 24. Then 180 ÷ 24 = 7.5 ft per man-hour.

questions.stem: A job takes 3 fitters 8 days. At the same rate, how long would 4 fitters take?
choices: 5 days
10.7 days
6.5 days
6 days
questions.explanation: The job is 3 × 8 = 24 man-days. 24 ÷ 4 = 6 days. More workers means fewer days — inverse relationship.

questions.stem: Schedule 40 pipe weighs 10.8 lb per foot. What does a 45 ft length weigh?
choices: 405 lb
462 lb
540 lb
486 lb

questions.stem: A 750-gallon tank is filled at 25 gallons per minute. How long does it take?
choices: 25 minutes
35 minutes
30 minutes
45 minutes
questions.explanation: 750 ÷ 25 = 30 minutes.

questions.stem: On a drawing scaled 1/4 in = 1 ft 0 in, a pipe run measures 3 1/2 in. What is the actual length?
choices: 14 ft
10 ft 6 in
7 ft
17 ft 6 in
questions.explanation: Every quarter inch is one foot, so each full inch is 4 ft. 3.5 × 4 = 14 ft.

questions.stem: A 55-gallon drum of cutting oil is 15% used. How much remains?
choices: 8.25 gal
40 gal
48.5 gal
questions.explanation: 15% of 55 is 8.25. 55 − 8.25 = 46.75 gal. Or take 85% of 55 directly.

questions.stem: A threading machine cuts 8 threads per inch. How many inches of pipe hold 120 threads?
choices: 12 in
960 in
16 in
15 in
questions.explanation: 120 ÷ 8 = 15 in. If you are tempted to multiply, check the units: threads ÷ threads-per-inch leaves inches.

questions.stem: An apprentice earns $22.40 an hour. In one week she works 40 regular hours plus 6 hours of overtime at time and a half. What is her gross pay?
A material list calls for elbows and tees in a 5 to 2 ratio. If the job uses 35 elbows, how many tees are needed?
questions.explanation: 35 ÷ 5 = 7 groups. Each group has 2 tees, so 7 × 2 = 14.

questions.stem: A pump moves 12 gallons per minute. How many gallons does it move in 2 hours 15 minutes?
questions.explanation: 2 hours 15 minutes = 135 minutes. 135 × 12 = 1,620 gallons. Convert to one unit before multiplying.

questions.stem: How many pieces 2 ft 8 in long can be cut from one 20 ft stick of pipe?
questions.explanation: 20 ft = 240 in and 2 ft 8 in = 32 in. 240 ÷ 32 = 7.5, and you cannot use half a piece, so 7.

questions.stem: A job was estimated at 480 labor hours and finished in 408. By what percent did the crew come in under estimate?
questions.explanation: The difference is 72 hours. 72 ÷ 480 = 0.15 = 15%. Divide by the estimate, not the actual.

questions.stem: One cubic foot holds about 7.48 gallons. Roughly how many gallons does a 10 cubic foot tank hold?
A steam line drops from 340 °F to 185 °F. What is the temperature drop?
A takeoff calls for 850 ft of pipe and the shop allows 6% for waste. How much waste is that?
choices: 42 ft
51 ft
48 ft
55 ft
questions.explanation: 6% of 850. One percent is 8.5, so six percent is 8.5 × 6 = 51 ft.

questions.stem: A glycol mix is made 3 parts water to 1 part glycol. In a 48-gallon batch, how much water is used?
choices: 12 gal
16 gal
32 gal
36 gal
questions.explanation: Three parts plus one part is four parts total. 48 ÷ 4 = 12 gal per part, and water is 3 parts: 36 gallons.

questions.stem: How long does it take to drive 54 miles at a steady 45 mph?
choices: 1 hr 05 min
1 hr 20 min
1 hr 12 min
1 hr 30 min
questions.explanation: 54 ÷ 45 = 1.2 hours. The 0.2 of an hour is 0.2 × 60 = 12 minutes, so 1 hr 12 min. Careful: 1.2 hours is not 1 hour 20 minutes.

questions.stem: A vessel is rated for 200 psi and its relief valve is set at 80% of that rating. If the gauge currently reads 145 psi, how far below the relief setting is it?
choices: 25 psi
15 psi
40 psi
55 psi
questions.explanation: Relief setting = 0.80 × 200 = 160 psi. 160 − 145 = 15 psi. Two steps — do not compare the gauge to the 200 psi rating.

questions.stem: Flow through a pipe follows Q = V × A, where V is velocity and A is the cross-sectional area. If the same flow passes from a 4-inch line into a 2-inch line, the velocity in the smaller line
choices: decreases
stays the same
increases
drops to zero
questions.explanation: Q is fixed. A gets smaller, so V must get larger to keep the product the same. That is rule 3: hold the result still and the two inputs trade off. This is why reducers make water move faster, not slower.

questions.stem: Fourteen pipe hangers cost $27.50 each. With 8% sales tax, what is the total?
A pipe has an outside diameter of 2.375 in and a wall thickness of 0.280 in. What is the inside diameter?
questions.explanation: The wall is subtracted twice, once on each side: 2.375 − (2 × 0.280) = 2.375 − 0.560 = 1.815 in.

questions.stem: For a 45° offset, travel equals run × 1.414. If the run is 16 in, what is the travel, to the nearest tenth?
questions.explanation: 16 × 1.414 = 22.624, which rounds to 22.6 in. On a 45° offset the travel is always longer than the run.

questions.stem: A tank drains from 900 gallons to 315 gallons in 45 minutes. What is the average drain rate?
choices: 20 gal/min
9 gal/min
15 gal/min
13 gal/min
questions.explanation: The drop is 900 − 315 = 585 gallons. 585 ÷ 45 = 13 gal/min.

questions.stem: Six fitters each work 9 1/2 hours on a shutdown. How many man-hours were spent?
questions.explanation: 6 × 9.5 = 57 man-hours.

questions.stem: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?
choices: Supervisors are responsible for locking out equipment on behalf of their crews.
Tags are an acceptable substitute for locks in most situations.
Valves should be replaced regularly because they leak.
Isolation means physically separating the energy source and locking it out individually, not simply shutting a valve.
questions.explanation: The whole passage builds one argument: closing a valve is not isolation, physical separation plus a personal lock is. The other choices each contradict something the passage says outright.

questions.stem: According to the passage, why is a closed valve not acceptable isolation?
choices: Valves leak, and someone may operate the handle without knowing a worker is downstream.
Valves are difficult to reach on most systems.
A valve cannot be fitted with a lock.
Valves are only rated for low pressure.
questions.explanation: Both reasons are stated directly: valves leak, and a handle can be turned by someone who does not know a fitter is on the other side. The passage never says a valve cannot accept a lock.

questions.stem: A worker who applied a personal lock has gone home for the day and the lock must come off. The passage requires
choices: the lock to remain until the worker returns, with no exceptions
a second lock to be added by the supervisor
any crew member to cut the lock and note it in the log
written authorization from the site supervisor plus a documented attempt to contact the worker
questions.explanation: The last two sentences state exactly this. "No exceptions" is too strong — the passage lays out a procedure for that situation rather than forbidding removal.

questions.stem: A foreman puts one lock on the isolation point on behalf of his five-man crew. Under this procedure, that is
choices: not acceptable, because a group hasp may never be used
not acceptable, because each worker must apply a personal lock
acceptable if the foreman also hangs a tag
acceptable, because the foreman is responsible for the crew
questions.explanation: The passage says a single lock applied by a supervisor on behalf of a crew does not satisfy the procedure. Group hasps are explicitly allowed — that is how five personal locks fit on one point.

questions.stem: The passage indicates that a tag used without a lock is permitted only when
choices: the isolating device cannot physically accept a lock, and a second safeguard is added
the system has already been bled to atmosphere
the work will last less than one shift
the supervisor signs the tag
questions.explanation: Both halves matter — the device must be incapable of accepting a lock, and a second independent safeguard is then required. A choice that gives only half the condition is not the answer.

questions.stem: Which of these does the passage identify as hot work?
choices: Grinding a weld
Pulling a vacuum on a line
Applying pipe dope to a threaded joint
Torquing a flange
questions.explanation: The opening sentence lists welding, cutting, brazing, grinding and soldering. Grinding throws sparks, which is why it counts.

questions.stem: How far does the required inspection radius extend around the work?
choices: 10 feet
35 feet
20 feet
60 feet
questions.explanation: Thirty-five feet in every direction, including below the work and behind partitions. The 60 in the passage is the fire watch time in minutes, not a distance.

questions.stem: After the last spark, the fire watch must remain for at least
choices: 60 minutes
30 minutes
15 minutes
the rest of the shift
questions.explanation: A minimum of 60 minutes, followed by one more walk of the area before leaving.

questions.stem: A fitter cuts pipe inside the shop's designated cutting bay. According to the passage, a written permit is
choices: required, but only if a fire watch is unavailable
not required, because the work is inside a designated area
required, because cutting always produces sparks
not required, because the work lasts less than one shift
questions.explanation: The passage states plainly that a permit is not required inside a designated area. Permit duration is tied to the shift and location named on it, but that is about permits that exist, not about whether one is needed.

questions.stem: Why does the passage single out work performed above open floor grating?
choices: Permits are not valid on elevated work platforms.
Fire blankets cannot be used on grating.
Sparks can travel farther than the cleared radius and fall to a lower level.
Grating cannot support a fire watch.
questions.explanation: The passage says sparks from overhead cutting travel well beyond 35 feet, and that openings must be sealed so sparks cannot drop to a lower level. Grating is an opening you cannot seal, so a containment plan is required.

questions.stem: In what order does the passage require the atmosphere to be tested?
choices: Toxic, oxygen, flammable
Oxygen, toxic, flammable
Flammable, oxygen, toxic
Oxygen, flammable, toxic
questions.explanation: Oxygen, then flammable gases and vapors, then toxic contaminants — a fixed order, stated directly.

questions.stem: Why is oxygen tested first?
choices: Combustible gas meters read accurately only within a normal oxygen range.
Ventilation cannot be started until oxygen is confirmed.
Oxygen deficiency is the most common hazard.
Oxygen readings take the longest to stabilize.
questions.explanation: The reason given is instrument accuracy: an oxygen-deficient or oxygen-enriched atmosphere makes the flammability reading unreliable. The other choices may sound sensible but the passage does not say them.

questions.stem: What oxygen content does the passage give as acceptable?
choices: 16.0 to 21.0 percent
20.9 percent exactly
19.5 to 23.5 percent
Below 10 percent of the lower explosive limit
questions.explanation: 19.5 to 23.5 percent. The 10 percent figure belongs to the flammable reading, not the oxygen reading — a classic swapped-detail distractor.

questions.stem: An attendant sees an entrant collapse at the bottom of a tank. Based on the passage, the attendant should
choices: enter immediately, since seconds matter
re-test the atmosphere before deciding
stay outside and summon the rescue team that was arranged before entry
enter only after donning a respirator
questions.explanation: The passage says the attendant never enters to perform a rescue, and explains why: most confined-space deaths are would-be rescuers. The rescue team and retrieval gear were arranged in advance precisely for this moment.

questions.stem: Readings are taken at the top, middle, and bottom of the space because
choices: the permit requires three separate signatures
gases differ in density, so some settle and others rise
instruments drift over the length of a hose
oxygen is always lowest at the bottom
questions.explanation: Stated directly at the end of the second paragraph. Saying oxygen is always lowest at the bottom overreaches — the passage says gases differ in density, not that one gas is always on the floor.

questions.stem: A 3-inch standard weight steel line carries liquid. What is the maximum hanger spacing?
choices: 7 ft
10 ft
17 ft
14 ft
questions.explanation: The schedule gives 14 ft for 3 in through 4 in carrying liquid.

questions.stem: A 6-inch line on the same job carries vapor rather than liquid. Maximum spacing is
choices: 19 ft
17 ft
14 ft
21 ft
questions.explanation: 17 ft for 6 in and larger, plus the 2 ft allowed for vapor service, gives 19 ft. This is a two-step reading question — find the base figure, then apply the modifier.

questions.stem: A trapeze hanger carrying three lines must be sized for
choices: one-fifth of the rod tensile strength
the total load of all lines running full of water
the total operating load of all three lines
the operating load of the heaviest line
questions.explanation: The specification is explicit: total load of all lines running full of water, not the operating load. The distractor reading “total operating load” is the trap; it changes a single word.

questions.stem: A copper tube run must hang from steel hangers. The specification allows this only with
choices: a shield or saddle at every contact point
a dielectric isolator or copper-plated hanger at every contact point
roller supports at every contact point
rods no smaller than 3/8 in
questions.explanation: Copper shall not contact ferrous hangers; the fix is a dielectric isolator or a copper-plated hanger. Shields and saddles belong to the insulation requirement, and rollers belong to the thermal movement requirement.

questions.stem: A line that will expand and contract in service must be supported so that
choices: the clevis hanger is oversized by one pipe size
supports are spaced 2 ft closer than the schedule
rods are sized at one-fifth of tensile strength
the pipe rests on rollers or slides, centered at the mid-point of its travel
questions.explanation: The last paragraph states both halves: rollers or slides instead of clevis hangers, positioned so the pipe sits centered at mid-travel. The one-fifth rod rule applies to every rod, not just thermal lines.

questions.stem: Why is hydrostatic testing preferred over pneumatic testing?
choices: Water is nearly incompressible, so a failure releases far less stored energy.
Pneumatic testing cannot reach 1.5 times design pressure.
Water finds leaks that gas cannot.
Water is cheaper than compressed gas.
questions.explanation: The stored-energy argument is the reason given. Pneumatic testing is not described as incapable of reaching test pressure — it is described as more dangerous when it fails.

questions.stem: The passage gives the normal test pressure and hold time as
choices: 1.25 times design pressure for 15 minutes
1.5 times operating pressure for 60 minutes
1.5 times design pressure for 30 minutes
2 times design pressure for 30 minutes
questions.explanation: 1.5 times the design pressure, held a minimum of 30 minutes. Note the wording — design pressure, not operating pressure.

questions.stem: Trapped air is vented before pressurizing because it
choices: corrodes the inside of the pipe
makes the gauge read high
defeats the safety advantage of water and can hide a slow leak
slows the filling of the system
questions.explanation: Both effects are stated: an air pocket stores energy the way a pneumatic test would, and it can hold the gauge steady while the line loses water.

questions.stem: The passage says a test gauge should be selected so that the test pressure falls
choices: at the top of the gauge range
anywhere on a calibrated gauge
in the middle third of the gauge range
just above the midpoint
questions.explanation: The middle third, because that is where a gauge reads most accurately. Calibration is also required, but it is not the whole requirement.

questions.stem: A relief valve rated below the test pressure is left in place when the system is pressurized. Based on the passage, this is a problem because
choices: relief valves cannot be recalibrated after a hydro test
the valve would prevent the system from being vented
the valve adds weight to the trapeze hangers
the valve is listed among the components that must be removed or isolated
questions.explanation: The third paragraph lists relief valves first among components that cannot take test pressure and must be removed or isolated. The other choices bring in ideas the passage never raises.

questions.stem: Gear A drives gear B. Which statement is correct?
choices: B turns at the same speed as A
B turns slower than A and in the same direction
B turns slower than A and in the opposite direction
B turns faster than A and in the same direction
questions.explanation: Meshed gears always turn opposite ways. The big gear turns slower: 12 teeth driving 36 teeth is a 3 to 1 reduction, so B makes one turn for every three of A. This is the classic trade-off — you give up speed to gain torque.

questions.stem: Gear A turns clockwise. Which way does gear C turn?
choices: It alternates
Counter-clockwise
It does not turn
Clockwise
questions.explanation: Each mesh reverses direction. A clockwise makes B counter-clockwise, and B counter-clockwise makes C clockwise. An odd number of gears in a train puts the last gear the same way as the first. The middle gear is an idler: it changes direction but not the overall speed ratio.

questions.stem: A chain runs from a 15-tooth drive sprocket to a 45-tooth driven sprocket. The driven sprocket turns
choices: one third as fast, opposite direction
one third as fast, same direction
three times as fast, same direction
three times as fast, opposite direction
questions.explanation: A chain drive keeps both sprockets turning the same way — unlike meshed gears. Tripling the tooth count cuts the speed to one third, and multiplies torque by three.

reduce the pressure at the far end
